title: Merge guard playbook (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for a lightweight 'merge guard' checklist and follow-ups when reviewing PRs in serving-runtime. This is purposely terse — copy bits into PR comments, post-merge tasks, or a proper Confluence page later.

Primary goals:
- Catch obvious regressions (perf, memory, correctness) before merge.
- Provide clear pre-merge gating and quick rollback/mitigation steps.
- Make reviewer feedback cheap to act on (concrete, reproducible).

Checklist (quick run every review):
1) Scope and intent
   - Does the PR description clearly state the user-visible change? (if not, ask for 1-line TL;DR that can go in release notes)
   - Is there a linked issue/Jira or a design doc? If not and the change is large, request a short design note.

2) Tests
   - Unit tests added/updated for new logic? If no, mark as TODO but allow small hotfixes to be merged with post-merge test follow-up.
   - Integration / e2e? For runtime perf or memory changes, require a perf regression test (even if coarse).

3) Safety nets
   - Feature flag? If risky, gate behind feature flag with default OFF and a rollout plan.
   - Config defaults: ensure sensible fallback values.

4) Performance quick-hit checks
   - Look for new synchronous I/O in hot paths (DB, network, fs).
   - Grep for common anti-patterns: regex to scan diff: "fetch\(|open\(|requests\.get\(|time\.sleep\(". If present, demand justification.
   - If change touches tokenizer, batching, kv-cache, or scheduling, request benchmark numbers (local bench ok for PR-level).

5) Memory / resource checks
   - New global caches? Ensure bounded size or eviction.
   - Large buffer allocations: are they pooled or per-request? Ask for per-request upper bound.

6) Observability
   - Add tracing spans / logs for new branches in runtime.
   - Metrics: counter for errors, histogram for latencies for the new code path.

7) Backwards compatibility
   - Config schema changes declared and migration steps included.

8) Security & secrets
   - No secrets in code. Any new KMS/HSM integration must include threat model note.

9) Deployment / rollout notes
   - Canary target size and success criteria (p50/p95 no worse than X% vs baseline, error increase < Y%).
   - Rollback criteria and how-to (rollback script, feature-flag toggle, pin to old model).

Quick commands to run locally (copy into PR):
- Run lightweight perf harness: 
  scripts/run_local_bench.sh --profile hotpath --rps 20 --duration 30s  # approximate
- Run unit tests touched by PR:
  tox -e py39 -- tests/test_foo.py::TestBar::test_baz
- Start minimal runtime: 
  export RD_ENV=local && make dev-run && curl -s 'http://localhost:8080/health'

Common reviewer comments (templates):
- Missing perf numbers: "Can you add a quick microbenchmark comparing the hotpath before/after? A simple script and the raw numbers (p50/p95) is fine for now."
- Observability ask: "Please add a trace/span around X so we can measure this in prod canaries."
- Safety net ask: "Can this be behind a feature flag initially? If not, please add more justification on why it's safe to roll without one."

Refactor ideas (non-blocking suggestions to seed follow-ups):
- Move request-prefetch logic into a helper with small public API (makes it easier to mock in unit tests).
- Extract the scheduling heuristics into a tiny policy interface so we can A/B different strategies during canary.
- Replace ad-hoc caching in module A with the shared bounded LRU util we've started elsewhere.

Post-merge follow-ups (tag in PR merge message):
- INF-XXXX: add perf dashboard for this route (owner: @Aisha)
- INF-YYYY: add e2e to nightly pipeline covering new config combos (owner: me)
- INF-ZZZZ: deprecate old flag/behavior after 4 weeks if canary stable

Rollback playbook (keep short):
1) If increase in p95 latency > 15% or errors > 2x baseline in canary for 10m:
   - Flip feature flag OFF or revert canary slice (k8s patch to scale down deployment)
   - Run quick smoke test: /health, run 5 sample requests, verify correctness
   - Open a hotfix PR with revert patch and notify on #serving-runtime channel
2) If issue only in some regions: route traffic away from region and escalate to infra if needed

Monitoring knobs to watch in first 2 hours after merge:
- request_count (route), errors_total, latency_histogram (p50/p95), worker_memory_rss, model_load_time
- Increase alert sensitivity for first 24h (lower thresholds by 10-20%)

Notes to self (todo rough list):
- build a tiny CLI to run the local perf harness with reproducible seed + output CSV (low priority).
- add a template PR checklist in the runtime repo that auto-populates with the items above (sync with @Diego).
- follow up with product on whether behavior change needs docs/upgrade notes.

Scratch examples to paste in PR comment:
- \"Quick perf note: ran scripts/run_local_bench.sh before and after; p95 increased from 82ms → 90ms (+9.8%). Seems acceptable under current SLA but let's watch canary for 24h.\"
- \"Observability: added span 'kv_cache.lookup' around cache hit path; please ensure sampling is OK for production.\"
- \"Rollback: this is behind feature flag 'new-sched-v2' and can be toggled via admin-console in case of issues.\"

Unresolved questions to ask author:
- Why choose a global static cache vs per-worker LRU? (concern: unbounded growth under X traffic)
- What's the expected QPS for the new path in production? (need to validate perf numbers scale)

End notes:
This is intentionally informal — copy/paste liberally. If something here proves useful, will migrate to a tiny repo-level PR template and link it from Confluence.

Changelog of this scratchpad:
- 2025-11-06: first draft (minimal checklist)
- 2025-12-02: added perf quick commands and rollback playbook
- 2026-02-17: expanded monitoring knobs and added post-merge follow-up examples

-- Luca M.
